model.name: sex-specific saturating binomial model
model.formula: p = p_max * (1 - exp(-k_f * female_per_ul)) * (1 - exp(-k_m * male_per_ul))

diagnostics.model_comparison: The sex-specific model has lower AIC and held-out log loss than the saturating total-gametocyte model.
diagnostics.asexual_assessment: Adding log10 asexual density changes neither held-out loss materially nor AIC favourably, so it is not retained.
diagnostics.calibration: Observed counts were compared with fitted binomial expectations across the probability range; sparse low-density feeds limit calibration assessment.

literature.claim: Female and male gametocyte densities jointly predict mosquito infection, with male limitation most apparent at low density.
literature.citation: Bradley et al., Predicting the likelihood and intensity of mosquito infection from sex specific Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte density, eLife, 2018.

literature.claim: SBP1, Pfs25, and PfMGET molecular assays have been used to distinguish circulating asexual, female, and male parasite streams.
literature.citation: Cao et al., Modeling the dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes in humans during malaria infection, eLife, 2019.

literature.claim: The relationship between gametocyte density and mosquito infection can be strongly nonlinear and feeding assays remain variable.
literature.citation: Churcher et al., Predicting mosquito infection from Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte density and estimating the reservoir of infection, eLife, 2013.
